title: Business Requirements Document — Requirements Chat 2

sections.title: 1. Executive Summary & Strategic Rationale
sections.body: The Hospital Management System (HMS) will provide a **centralized, role‑based platform** for managing all core hospital operations—including patient registration, clinical workflows, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, inventory, and staff management. By consolidating disparate processes into a single, secure web‑based solution, the hospital aims to improve care coordination, reduce administrative overhead, accelerate patient throughput, and ensure compliance with **HIPAA**, **GDPR**, **HL7 FHIR**, and **DICOM** standards.

sections.title: 2. Business Objectives & Success Metrics
sections.body:
- **Objective 1:** Reduce patient appointment wait time by 30%.
- **Objective 2:** Achieve >99.5% billing accuracy and reduce claim rejections.
- **Objective 3:** Attain 100% compliance with HIPAA and GDPR audit requirements.
- **Objective 4:** Maintain system availability ≥99.9% (high‑availability architecture).
- **Objective 5:** Meet disaster‑recovery targets **RTO < 1 hour** and **RPO < 5 minutes**.

**Success Metrics**
| Metric | Target |
|--------|--------|
| Average appointment scheduling time | ≤ 2 minutes |
| EMR data entry error rate | ≤ 0.1% |
| Audit‑log immutability compliance | 100% of logs immutable per HIPAA §164.312(b) |
| Encryption of PHI at rest | AES‑256 for all databases |
| System uptime | ≥ 99.9% per SLA |

sections.title: 3. Scope & Operational Boundaries (In/Out of Scope)
sections.body:
**In‑Scope**
- Patient registration and profile management
- Appointment scheduling, queue management, and doctor availability
- OPD/IPD workflow (admission, transfer, discharge)
- Electronic Medical Records (diagnosis, prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes)
- Laboratory test ordering and reporting
- Pharmacy prescription processing and medicine inventory
- Bed and ward management
- Billing, payments, insurance claim processing, invoicing, receipts
- Staff management and role‑based access control (Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, Accountant, Patient)
- Patient and clinician portals with dashboards, notifications, search/filter, reporting, audit logs
- Data backup/recovery, audit trail immutability, security controls (HTTPS, JWT/OAuth, password encryption, session management)
- Deployment on cloud or on‑premise using the specified technology stack (React/Next.js, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot, PostgreSQL/MySQL, Redis)

**Out‑of‑Scope**
- Tele‑medicine video conferencing modules
- AI‑driven diagnostic decision support
- Integration with external medical devices not covered by HL7 FHIR/DICOM
- Third‑party patient engagement mobile apps (beyond the web portal)
- Legacy system data migration (assumed to be handled separately)

sections.title: 4. Key Stakeholders & Governance Personas
sections.body:
- **Hospital Executive Sponsor** – overall funding and strategic alignment
- **Chief Medical Officer (CMO)** – clinical workflow validation
- **Chief Information Officer (CIO) / IT Operations** – infrastructure, security, compliance
- **Compliance Officer** – HIPAA/GDPR audit and policy enforcement
- **Doctors** – primary users of clinical dashboards and EMR
- **Nurses** – nursing notes, vital signs, medication administration
- **Receptionists** – patient intake and appointment scheduling
- **Pharmacists** – pharmacy inventory and prescription dispensing
- **Lab Technicians** – test ordering and result entry
- **Accountants / Billing Staff** – invoicing, insurance claims, financial reporting
- **Patients / Guardians** – portal access to personal health information
- **Procurement / Inventory Managers** – supply chain and inventory control

sections.title: 5. Business Requirements Specification Matrix
table: Capture demographic, insurance, and consent data for new patients.
System creates a patient record within 2 minutes; all mandatory fields validated; data stored encrypted at rest (AES‑256).
Enforce least‑privilege access for all defined roles.
Access matrix matches role definitions; unauthorized access attempts logged and blocked; audit logs immutable per HIPAA §164.312(b).
Allow patients and staff to book, modify, and cancel appointments with real‑time doctor availability.
Appointment created/updated in <3 seconds; conflict detection prevents double‑booking; notifications sent to patient portal.
Maintain complete clinical records including diagnoses, prescriptions, allergies, vital signs, and nursing notes.
All entries searchable; version history retained; data exportable in HL7 FHIR format; audit trail records every change.
Enable clinicians to order tests and receive results electronically.
Test order submitted and visible to lab staff within 5 seconds; results uploaded and viewable by ordering clinician within defined turnaround time.
Track medicine stock levels, expirations, and dispensing.
Inventory counts updated in real time; low‑stock alerts generated; batch/lot traceability maintained per FDA/DICOM guidelines.
Generate invoices, process payments, and submit insurance claims.
Invoice generated at discharge; payment status reflected instantly; claim submission conforms to HIPAA transaction standards.
Provide patients access to appointments, prescriptions, reports, and bills.
Patients can log in via secure HTTPS; view up‑to‑date information; session expires after 15 minutes of inactivity.
Perform regular encrypted backups and enable rapid restoration.
Backups performed nightly; RTO < 1 hour, RPO < 5 minutes; backup data encrypted with AES‑256 and stored off‑site.
Capture immutable logs of all system actions for compliance reporting.
Logs written to append‑only store; tamper‑evidence meets HIPAA audit‑log requirements; reports exportable for regulator review.

sections.title: 6. Assumptions & Operational Constraints
sections.body:
- The system will be deployed on infrastructure that supports TLS 1.2+ and AES‑256 encryption at rest.
- Users will access the application via modern browsers (Chrome, Edge, Firefox) on desktop or tablet devices.
- Network latency within the hospital campus is assumed to be < 100 ms.
- Integration points (e.g., external lab equipment) will conform to HL7 FHIR or DICOM standards where needed.
- All PHI handling must comply with **HIPAA** Security Rule and **GDPR** Article 32 (security of processing).
- The project will use the technology stack outlined in the source excerpt; any deviation requires formal change control.
- Staffing levels for support and maintenance are assumed to be sufficient to meet the 1‑hour RTO target.

sections.title: 7. Risk & Compliance Baseline
sections.body:
- **Compliance Frameworks:** HIPAA (Security Rule, Privacy Rule), GDPR (if EU patients), HL7 FHIR, DICOM.
- **Non‑Functional Benchmarks:** PHI encryption at rest (AES‑256), audit‑trail immutability, RTO < 1 hour, RPO < 5 minutes, system availability ≥ 99.9%.
- **Identified Risks:** None reported in the audit findings.
- **Mitigation Strategy:** Continuous compliance monitoring, periodic security assessments, and adherence to the listed benchmarks will be embedded in the development lifecycle.

--- Page 1 ---
Hospital Management System 
A Hospital Management System (HMS)  should provide a centralized platform for 
managing hospital operations, patient information, medical records, appointments, doctors, 
nurses, staff, billing, pharmacy, laboratory, and inventory. The system should support  role-
based access  for Admin, Doctor, Nurse, Receptionist, Pharmacist, Lab Technician, 
Accountant, and Patient. Core requirements should include patient registration and profile 
management, appointment scheduling and queue management, doctor availability, O PD/IPD 
management, admission/discharge/transfer, electronic medical records, diagnosis, 
prescriptions, treatment history, allergies, vital signs, nursing notes, laboratory test requests 
and reports, pharmacy prescriptions and medicine inventory, bed/ward m anagement, billing 
and payments, insurance management, invoices and receipts, hospital expenses, staff 
management, and inventory/procurement. Patients should be able to view appointments, 
prescriptions, reports, bills, and medical history through a portal,  while doctors should have 
dashboards for appointments, patient records, diagnosis, prescriptions, and clinical notes. 
The system should also provide  dashboards, notifications, search/filtering, reports, audit 
logs, data validation, backup/recovery, security, and role -based authorization . 
Functional requirements should cover complete workflows such as  patient registration → 
appointment → consultation → diagnosis → laboratory/pharmacy → billing → follow -
up, and admission → bed allocation → treatment → investigations → discharge → final 
billing. Non -functional requirements should include responsive web UI, scalability, high 
availability, fast API responses , secure authentication, password encryption, session 
management, HTTPS, database integrity, auditability, privacy of medical information, error 
handling, logging, and regular backups. A suitable architecture can use  React/Next.js for 
frontend, FastAPI/Node.js/Spring Boot for backend, PostgreSQL/MySQL for database, 
REST APIs, JWT/OAuth-based authentication, Redis for caching/queues, and cloud or 
on-premise deployment , with separate modules for  Authentication, Patients, 
Appointments, EMR, Doctors, Nursing, L aboratory, Pharmacy, Billing, Inventory, 
Staff, Reports, Notifications, and Administration.
